question.problem: An air compressor moves $\frac{8}{15}$ gallons of air in four seconds. Find the unit rate of gallons per second.
question.worked_solution:
To compute the unit rate of gallons per second, we divide the number of gallons, $\frac{8}{15},$ by the number of seconds, $4$, as follows:   

$$
\frac{8}{15}÷4
$$

Dividing a fraction by a whole number is equivalent to multiplying the fraction by the reciprocal of that whole number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{15}÷4 & =\frac{8}{15}÷\frac{4}{1} \\  & =\frac{8}{15}\times \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{8\times 1}{15\times 4} \\  & =\frac{2\times 4}{15\times 4} \\  & =\frac{2\times \cancel{4}}{15\times \cancel{4}} \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit rate in this situation is $\frac{2}{15}$ gallons per second.
